profile.name: Fal
profile.description: Fal (fal.ai) is a generative media platform that provides developers and enterprises with instant access to a vast library of over 1,000 production‑ready image, video, audio, and 3D AI models via a unified API. The service offers serverless, on‑demand GPU compute—including H100, H200, and B200 instances—so users can run, fine‑tune, or deploy custom models without managing infrastructure. Fal’s proprietary Inference Engine delivers up to 10× faster diffusion model performance, supporting scaling from a single request to millions of daily calls with 99.99% uptime. The platform also supplies dedicated clusters for large‑scale training, enterprise‑grade security, SOC 2 compliance, and 24/7 support, enabling companies to embed state‑of‑the‑art generative AI into products quickly and cost‑effectively.

benchmarks.name: Cluely
benchmarks.why: Fast, meme-style hooks and punchy AI-demo clips that get shared widely; the format of showing an AI tool doing something impressive in seconds transfers to fal's model demos.

benchmarks.name: Cal AI
benchmarks.why: Creator-led UGC where a real person reacts to the app on camera with a clear before-and-after result, driving app sign-ups; transfers to developer creators showing a model output and saying what it cost or how fast it ran.

plan.scout_notes: Mostly off-topic: the results are AI music, dance, "fall" clips, a GPU price joke, and AI-art/short-drama channels, so almost none are developers buying compute. Breakouts (views far above followers) include jc_cripin (2,704x), icecreamwaffles87 (1,115x) and gage_sampson (173x, 16.5M views), but none is about generative media APIs. Selling signals are weak: leo925579 (Higgsfield short drama, whop purchase link), askgrok (Grok Imagine API CTA, "try it today in the API") and the app-builder clips hustlewithgianni and graciejcreates, which have high saves per like (0.84 and 0.79) and carry the developer-builder audience. Missing: any face-to-camera developer testimonial or 'I tried' review of an image/video/audio API, and any Fal, Replicate or Together comparison.

brand.name: fal (Private Deployments)
brand.one_liner: fal is a platform where developers call over a thousand image, video, audio and 3D AI models through one API, and rent GPUs to run or train their own models.
value_props: One unified API for image, video, audio, 3D and world models
Integrate new models without managing separate providers
Swap models by changing only the endpoint ID
Deploy custom models on serverless inference that autoscales from zero to thousands of GPUs
Built-in observability to monitor production inference
Compute clusters of H100, H200, B200 and B300 GPUs for training and fine-tuning
brand.tone: Confident, technical and developer-first. Short punchy lines like "zero headaches" and "just plug in and generate".
brand.visual_style: Dark, modern developer-style look with a code editor, model cards with sample media, and hot-pink (#ec084d) accents on black and white.
brand.product_look: A dark landing page headed "Your full stack for generative media" with three product blocks (Model APIs, Serverless, Compute), a tabbed grid of model cards with sample images and video, and a code editor showing a TypeScript fal.subscribe snippet. Get Started and Contact Sales buttons.
proof_points: Access to 1,500+ generative media models through one API (site)
Autoscaling across thousands of GPUs for custom models (site)
GPU clusters: H100, H200, B200, B300 (site)
Cited by ChatGPT as a top default for production FLUX and video generation APIs

content_patterns.pattern: Surprising capability claim as the hook, then a fast demo with the visual changing about every 2 seconds
content_patterns.why_it_works: The bold claim stops the scroll. The constantly changing visual panel keeps the eye moving while the presenter explains a simple flow.

content_patterns.pattern: Numbered, copyable steps that end with striking generated output
content_patterns.why_it_works: Viewers save it as a recipe and the output shows the payoff. Short imperative steps feel easy.

content_patterns.pattern: Setup-friction objection answered in one line, then a single concrete ask
content_patterns.why_it_works: Developers drop off when setup looks hard. A one-line answer and one clear next step convert.

concept.why: The reference is a Runway Meta ad that ran 22 days and is still running, with a 'Sign up' button and a comment-for-link ask. That is the strongest conversion evidence in the set. It has a cloneability of 7.6/10 and runs 30.6 s, within the 45 s budget, with one static presenter in one continuous take. Fit is 7/10: a dev-tool demo suits the split layout. The screen-recording top panel is replaced by fal's real site screenshots, which keeps the layout without laying the product over someone else's screen. The other references are weaker: ref_be7c733d59 is only 4.6 cloneable and ref_29d48c6809 is 4.7 with 65% screen time and a money claim fal can't support.

notes: lint: 7 beats vs the reference's 1: keep its beats one for one (merging middle beats is fine when shortening)
lint: hook beat is 4.5s vs the reference's 30.6s

Beat 5 "No separate integration per provider, no GPUs to manage." is shown over s3, the docs page, with no screen text. The docs page doesn't show either claim. When filming, the edit should lay a short "1 API / 0 GPUs to manage" card over the docs shot. Otherwise the visual doesn't back up the words.

Every beat is tagged [excited]. The reference is upbeat but varies, so the objection beat should be [matter-of-fact] or [deadpan]. The beat 4 question should be [curious]. This is a delivery note, not a rewrite.

The reference is a single hook beat and this script has 7. The creative brief asks for the reference's selling beats in order (hook, demo, objection, click ask), and the cut rhythm of about 3 s matches the reference's roughly 1.9 s cuts, so the extra beats are acceptable. The added serverless beat is the only new beat and is grounded in the brief.

Line lengths fit their seconds (about 190-200 wpm). The runtime is about 23 s against a 24 s target. The hook wording stays close to the reference, and the hook flows into "you just paste a few lines of code."

issues: The presenter's face, hair, black tee and background stay the same across all 4 frames, so identity is consistent.
The camera angle is slightly low and close, with a mild wide-angle look at the edges. It is not heavy distortion.
The lighting is evening LED, not the 'natural daylight' in the prompt. This fits the setting description and isn't a problem.
The background has a lamp, a shelf with items and a plant, so it is a little more cluttered than 'no clutter'. Minor.
The mouth shapes in frames 1 and 3 are a bit wide, and the smile in frame 3 is fairly big. Both stay within natural speech and are not cartoonish.
The presenter's hands are out of frame, there are no screens or text, and the product is correctly absent.
Frame 2: both hands/fingertips rise into the bottom of the frame as a gesture. They are blurry and cropped, so they are not clearly malformed. The brief asked for hands mostly below the frame.
Frame 1 and frame 3: the face is a bit close and wide-angle, with slight perspective distortion. It is not heavy.
The lighting is evening purple LED, not the 'natural daylight' in the prompt. This matches the setting description, so it is minor.
The mouth shapes are slightly broad in frame 2 (big grin) and frame 1 (stretched). They are still within natural excited speech.
The product is correctly absent, and no on-screen text or readable screens are visible. The identity, room and shirt stay consistent across the frames.
Frame 4 has a blurry partial hand or thumb at the bottom edge. It is only briefly visible and reads as a natural gesture, but it is slightly ambiguous.
Frame 4 has his eyes closed. This looks like a blink or a mid-speech beat, not most of the shot.
Framing and head size shift a little between frames, and frame 1 looks slightly wider-angle. The identity stays the same.
The background has a lamp, shelves and a dark monitor edge, so it is a little less minimal than 'no clutter'. Nothing on it is readable.
The lighting is stylized purple LED with a soft studio feel, not natural daylight. It suits the evening home-office brief.

Frame 1: the mouth is open very wide with the tongue showing and the eyebrows raised. This is more exaggerated than the casual-conversation mouth the brief asks for, though it could pass as an excited word like "Tap".

Frame 2: the eyes are closed in a big smile, which looks like a blink or smile moment. A blurry hand or fingers also drift into the bottom-left corner, which goes against "hands out of frame". Because it is soft and brief, it is minor.
Frame 1 is framed slightly closer to the lens than the other frames, and the face looks a bit wider. This is a small framing change and the identity still looks consistent.
The lighting is a purple and pink LED evening look rather than natural daylight. This matches the stated setting.
There is no product, on-screen text or readable screen, which is correct for a presenter-only shot.
